extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines various multiple procedure payment reductions (MPPR). Practitioner reimbursement for a procedure code generally includes reimbursement for the individual costs, also known as inputs, typically associated with that service. For example, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) uses a formula that accounts for the inputs associated with a procedure code to determine Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) reimbursement rates for that code. When the same provider renders multiple services, or multiple units of the same service, to the same patient on the same day, the total calculation for the procedure code(s) could account more than once for an input that was only rendered once. Examples of inputs that might be contemplated in reimbursement for certain procedure codes, that would not typically be duplicated in the same encounter include: greeting and gowning the patient; preparing the room, equipment and supplies; providing education and obtaining consent. An MPPR adjusts reimbursement to offset duplication of reimbursement for inputs that were only rendered once.

extracted_content.content: Neither multiple endoscopy reduction nor multiple surgery reduction could apply to the service. If multiple endoscopy reduction applies, it is always determined before multiple surgery reduction. After determining any multiple endoscopy reductions, all endoscopic services in the same endoscopic family are treated as a single service for the purpose of determining multiple surgery reduction, as follows:

extracted_content.title: Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.content: For multiple surgery reduction ranking purposes, endoscopic procedures in the same endoscopic family are treated as one service.

extracted_content.content: An endoscopic family's multiple surgery reduction ranking establishes the multiple surgery reduction percentage, if any, for all services in that endoscopic family. Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a unit of a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments.

Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that includes, among other information, multiple procedure indicator, relative value units and conversion factors for practitioner services. This file is commonly referred to as the relative value unit (RVU) table. Elements of the file that are referenced in this policy include the following:

CF: The conversion factor is the amount shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year.

PE GPCI: The practice expense geographic price index for the area where the service was rendered, shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year.

PE RVU: The practice expense relative value unit is the amount shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year.

Modifiers X{EPSU}: Modifiers XE, XP, XS and XU, collectively.

Modifier XE: Separate encounter.

Modifier XP: Separate practitioner.

Modifier XS: Separate structure.

Modifier XU: Unusual non-overlapping service.

Practice Expense (PE): One of three groups of inputs used to determine pricing of services covered under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS); PE accounts for costs of running a practice (other than expenses associated with professional liability and the practitioner's actual work), including rent, equipment, supplies and staff costs other than the work performed by the practitioner personally.

Professional Component (PC): The professional component of a service is for practitioner work interpreting a diagnostic test or performing a procedure and includes indirect practice and malpractice expenses related to that work.

Same Provider: A single qualified practitioner or multiple practitioners within the same group practice.

Technical Component (TC): The technical component of a service is for all non-practitioner work and includes administrative, personnel and capital (equipment and facility) costs and related malpractice expenses.
